nodes.content: Design distributed training recovery that preserves optimizer and data progress consistency across failures and worker membership changes.
requirements: Recovered executions match failure-free optimizer-update and sample-consumption histories, including failures during resharding.
Recovery adds at most 5% failure-free step latency versus identical training without recovery support.

nodes.content: Use deterministic sample IDs and reductions, pipelined durable step journals, checkpoint replay, and epoch-fenced atomic resharding.
How can step journals and ownership fences prevent duplicate updates or samples when a worker crashes mid-reshard?
Epoch-fenced step-journal commits and deterministic sample-ID replay preserve identical update hashes and sample-ID sequences across mid-reshard crashes.
Implement fenced commits; crash 8→12-worker reshard phases; compare update hashes, sample sequences, and p95 step latency against uninterrupted baseline.
Run 100 ReshardCrash-8to12 trials with crashes during shard transfer and commit; compare update hashes and sample IDs against baseline.
In 100/100 ReshardCrash-8to12 trials, update hashes and sample-ID sequences matched uninterrupted 8→12-worker runs exactly.
Select fenced commits and deterministic replay because all 100 crash trials matched baseline histories; verify ≤5% latency before deployment.
ReshardCrash-8to12 trace bundle records 100 crash schedules, journal epochs, update hashes, and ordered sample IDs alongside baseline comparisons.
Durable journal-tail acknowledgment before an epoch-fenced ownership swap prevents duplicate or missing updates and samples during reshard crashes.
Replay ReshardCrash-8to12 traces, kill owners around journal-tail acknowledgment and epoch swap, then compare update and sample histories.
In 3/40 targeted replays, crashes after durable tail acknowledgment but before epoch-fenced swap skipped one update: cursor outpaced optimizer checkpoint.
Extend selected fenced commits to atomically journal optimizer deltas with sample cursors; retest reshard crashes and ≤5% latency.
Implement atomic step records binding optimizer deltas to sample cursors, then inject crashes across acknowledgment, checkpoint, and ownership-swap boundaries.
AtomicStepJournal v2 commits optimizer deltas and sample cursors together, replaying uncheckpointed records before epoch-fenced ownership swaps.
Group-commit atomic optimizer-delta/sample-cursor records before update visibility; snapshot incrementally off-thread to target ≤5% p95 step-latency overhead.
Benchmark v2 group commits and background snapshots; verify identical update/sample histories and ≤5% p95 latency overhead against recovery-free runs.
Benchmark AtomicStepJournal v2 through 8→12-worker crashes, comparing basic journaling and group-commit snapshots against recovery-free histories and p95 latency.
Across 100 reshard crashes, group commits matched update hashes/sample sequences; p95 latency rose 3.8% versus recovery-free, basic journaling 8.1%.
Can group commits and off-thread snapshots keep p95 overhead ≤5% under repeated membership changes while preserving atomic replay?
With overlapping snapshots and bounded commit batches, repeated 8↔12-worker resharding retains exact histories at ≤5% p95 overhead.
Stress AtomicStepJournal v2 through 50 crash-injected 8↔12-worker reshardings; verify update hashes/sample IDs and benchmark crash-free p95 against recovery-disabled runs.
Off-thread incremental snapshots produced torn checkpoints in 2/50 reshardings; pinned overlapping snapshots and bounded commits preserved histories, 4.6% overhead.
Adopt AtomicStepJournal v2 with pinned overlapping snapshots and bounded group commits: exact histories at 4.6% p95 overhead.
Revise benchmark to pin overlapping snapshots and bound group commits; retest repeated 8↔12-worker crash replay and ≤5% p95 overhead.
Configure v2 pinned overlapping snapshots and ≤2-ms/16-record commits; replay 100 crash-injected 8↔12 reshardings, checking histories and baseline p95.
AtomicStepJournal v2 benchmark bundle contains 100 reshard-crash schedules, pinned-snapshot manifests, update/sample comparisons, and recovery-disabled p95 traces.
Bind immutable sample ranges to logical steps, then transfer versioned optimizer shards behind quorum-fenced handoff manifests.
Implement step-bound sample ranges and quorum-fenced shard manifests atop AtomicStepJournal v2; crash-test histories and ≤5% p95 overhead.
Replay the AtomicStepJournal v2 benchmark bundle after implementing step-bound ranges and quorum handoffs; compare histories and p95 overhead.
All 100 reshard-crash replays matched baseline update hashes and sample ranges; p95 step overhead was 4.8%.
ShardHandoff v1 adds step-bound sample-range leases and quorum-fenced optimizer-shard manifests to AtomicStepJournal v2.
Use virtual-rank gradient reductions and journaled per-step RNG counters to preserve update hashes across worker-count changes.
Can virtual-rank reductions and journaled RNG counters preserve bitwise update hashes when worker membership changes mid-step?
Fixed virtual-rank reduction trees and step-keyed RNG counters yield identical update hashes despite 8→12-worker mid-step crashes.
Inject 100 mid-step 8→12-worker crashes with virtual-rank reductions and step-keyed RNG; compare update hashes against uninterrupted runs.
Step-keyed counters diverged in 4/100 crashes; journaled per-microbatch dropout counters restored 100/100 matching virtual-rank update hashes.
VirtualRankReplay v1 fixes gradient reduction order and journals per-microbatch dropout counters for deterministic mid-step replay.
Use replayable prefetch queues keyed by logical-step sample ranges; advance consumption only with committed optimizer records.
Implement step-keyed prefetch replay with commit-gated cursors; test crashes during resharding for exact sample histories and ≤5% latency overhead.
Integrate ShardHandoff v1 and VirtualRankReplay v1 with commit-gated prefetch; crash-test 8↔12 reshardings, comparing update hashes, sample IDs, and p95 latency.
Across 100 crash-injected 8↔12 reshardings, commit-gated prefetch matched failure-free update hashes and sample-ID sequences; p95 overhead was 4.9%.
Adopt commit-gated prefetch with ShardHandoff v1 and VirtualRankReplay v1’s microbatch counters: exact crash histories, 4.9% p95 overhead.
Package adopted recovery stack, then validate exact update/sample histories under compound crashes and ≤5% recovery-disabled p95 latency overhead.
Using the v2 benchmark bundle, integrate ShardHandoff v1, VirtualRankReplay v1, and commit-gated prefetch; compare compound-crash histories and recovery-disabled p95.
RecoveryStack v1 bundles AtomicStepJournal v2, ShardHandoff v1, VirtualRankReplay v1, commit-gated prefetch, and compound-crash benchmark scripts.
